sub_scenario.family: prepared public representation versus live improvised exposure
sub_scenario.one_line: university admissions director: yes only with collected questions and a moderator

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the policy summary and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The question archive review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Prospective-family campus tours, unscripted all day, are a pleasure.
Unscripted narrative settings are fine.
Narrative is safe ground.
Someone new shadowed me in the admissions office this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the forum formats into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
The prepared town halls run cleanly: questions collected ahead, answers checked against policy, and the archive shows zero corrections across four cycles.
The collected-question format has a spotless record.
Spotless and archived.
Written question-and-answer columns in the newsletter go smoothly every cycle.
The written channel behaves.
It always has.
I archived last cycle's notes on the question archive and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
Admissions policy language is legally sensitive; our counsel flags improvised policy statements as the top institutional risk in my role.
Counsel has named the specific hazard.
Named it in the annual risk memo.
A vendor call about the policy summary ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the admissions office checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the forum formats.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the question archive records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The one open-microphone live-streamed forum we ran produced my misstatement of the deferral policy, which trended locally and took a formal statement to correct.
One open microphone, one trending correction.
Trending is the part I cannot un-live.
I sketched next week's plan for the forum formats before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the policy summary updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The trustees want me fronting this year's forum and are asking my format terms this week.
The terms window is open now.
Open, and it will not reopen.
A trustee says scripted forums feel evasive and families deserve spontaneity.
Spontaneity framing.
Framing that ignores the deferral incident.
I closed the week by updating the admissions office handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The trustees want me fronting the admissions forum. What conditions should my yes carry?
